root_cause.text: `rds_ib_send_unmap_op()` in the RDS/IB send completion path failed to recognize masked atomic work request opcodes, so `rds_ib_xmit_atomic()`-submitted completions returned `NULL` for `rm` while `send->s_op` remained set, leading `rds_ib_send_cqe_handler()` to dereference a null `rds_message` pointer.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE says `rds_ib_xmit_atomic()` always uses masked opcodes (`IB_WR_MASKED_ATOMIC_CMP_AND_SWP` / `IB_WR_MASKED_ATOMIC_FETCH_AND_ADD`), but `rds_ib_send_unmap_op()` “only handles the non-masked opcodes,” causing masked completions to “falls through to default and returns rm == NULL while send->s_op is left set,” after which `rds_ib_send_cqe_handler()` dereferences `rm->m_final_op`; the patch fixes this by adding the two masked opcodes to the same `case` block as `IB_WR_ATOMIC_FETCH_AND_ADD` and `IB_WR_ATOMIC_CMP_AND_SWP`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add masked atomic verbs to the atomic unmap path so their completion handling works correctly.
intent_record.what: Two additional switch cases were added in rds_ib_send_unmap_op(): IB_WR_MASKED_ATOMIC_FETCH_AND_ADD and IB_WR_MASKED_ATOMIC_CMP_AND_SWP now fall through to the same atomic send unmap handling as IB_WR_ATOMIC_FETCH_AND_ADD and IB_WR_ATOMIC_CMP_AND_SWP.
intent_record.how: Masked atomic work requests are now treated as atomic operations during completion/unmap processing, so their associated RDS atomic message state is cleaned up correctly instead of being skipped or handled by a different path.

grouping_result.intent: Add masked atomic verbs to the atomic unmap path so their completion handling works correctly.

relevance_review.reason: The change explicitly adds masked atomic verbs to the atomic unmap/completion path, which directly matches the root cause where masked atomic opcodes were not recognized and led to a null rds_message dereference.

candidates.rationale: The vulnerable completion-path switch only handled the unmasked atomic opcodes here; masked atomic work requests were not recognized, so their completions fell through without converting send->s_op into the corresponding rds_message, eventually leading to a NULL dereference in completion handling.
This is the other pre-fix atomic opcode case in the switch. Because only these exact opcodes were handled, masked atomic completions were missed, leaving send->s_op set while rm remained NULL.

This dereference gate assumed the switch had correctly identified the atomic request. When masked atomic opcodes were not matched, the code path failed to establish rm from send->s_op, making later completion handling unsafe.

vuln_statements.explanation: The pre-fix atomic-unmap switch only recognized the unmasked atomic opcode here, so masked atomic work requests were not translated into an rds_message and later completion handling could dereference NULL.

This is the second unmasked atomic opcode handled by the vulnerable switch. Because masked atomic variants were absent, completions for those requests bypassed the rm setup path and left send->s_op set.

This guard relied on the switch having identified the atomic send correctly. When masked atomic opcodes were missed, send->s_op remained set without a valid rm, enabling the NULL dereference in completion handling.

The shown function bodies include the send completion path, especially `rds_ib_send_cq_comp_handler()` and `rds_ib_send_unmap_rm()`, but they do not show the vulnerable construct described in the root cause. In this commit, completions are classified only with `switch (send->s_wr.opcode)` and the code expects `IB_WR_SEND`, `IB_WR_RDMA_WRITE`, or `IB_WR_RDMA_READ`:

- `switch (send->s_wr.opcode) { case IB_WR_SEND: if (send->s_rm) rds_ib_send_unmap_rm(ic, send, wc.status); break; case IB_WR_RDMA_WRITE: case IB_WR_RDMA_READ: ... }`

There is no masking logic such as `opcode & IB_WR_OPCODE_MASK`, and there is also no dereference of `send->s_op` after a `NULL` message pointer in the shown code. The atomic/RDMA completion special handling present here is:

- `if (unlikely(wc.status == IB_WC_REM_ACCESS_ERR && send->s_op)) { ... rm = rds_send_get_message(conn, send->s_op); if (rm) rds_ib_send_rdma_complete(rm, wc.status); }`

This is a guarded lookup, not the null-dereference scenario from the vulnerability description. So the vulnerable construct is absent in this commit version, and the fix for masked atomic opcodes is not present either, but cannot be assessed as already fixed from this snippet alone.

bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable construct is not present in this commit. The root cause says `rds_ib_send_unmap_op()` failed to recognize masked atomic work request opcodes, causing atomic completions to leave `send->s_op` set while `rm` was NULL. In this snippet, atomic handling is explicitly present and routed through `rds_ib_send_unmap_op()`: `case IB_WR_ATOMIC_FETCH_AND_ADD:` and `case IB_WR_ATOMIC_CMP_AND_SWP:` both do `if (send->s_op) { rm = container_of(send->s_op, struct rds_message, atomic); rds_ib_send_unmap_atomic(ic, send->s_op, wc_status); }`. The completion path also avoids dereferencing a NULL `rm` because it only dereferences after `if (&send->s_op == &rm->m_final_op)`, and `rm` is only used after being assigned by `rds_ib_send_unmap_op()`. The older buggy pattern from the root cause—atomic completions relying on `send->s_rm` and failing when the opcode was masked—is absent here because `send->s_rm` has been removed and the code uses `send->s_op` plus explicit atomic opcode cases. Therefore this commit already contains the fix and does not contain the vulnerable construct.

bic_trace_step.reason: The relevant completion-path logic is present, and this version already avoids the vulnerable NULL-dereference pattern. The old code used a message pointer from the send work ("send->s_rm") and only set it in a special atomic-only case; the new code replaces that with per-op tracking and only unmaps/completes when an op pointer exists: "if (send->s_op) { rm = container_of(send->s_op, struct rds_message, atomic); rds_ib_send_unmap_atomic(...); }". In the CQ handler, it now uses "rm = rds_ib_send_unmap_op(ic, send, wc.status);" and guards message teardown with "if (&send->s_op == &rm->m_final_op) { ... rds_message_unmapped(rm); rds_message_put(rm); send->s_op = NULL; }". This indicates the fix is already in place: atomic completions are handled via the op pointer, not by assuming a separate message pointer, and there is no vulnerable dereference of a NULL rds_message pointer in this shown code.
